search.query: The actual search keywords or phrase, excluding the search command, requested content category and supported explicit filters. Null for a filter-only search. Preserve ordinary uses of in/from and dates within the topic; do not turn them into filters.
search.search_scope: The exact noun phrase naming the requested content category: messages, channels, DMs, documents, files, notes, tasks, emails, calls, folders, agents, AI chats, calendar events or events. Null when no category is specified. Category words inside the search topic are not a scope. Return a span from the draft, not a canonical category name.
search.search_from: Names or supplied addresses explicitly requested as message senders, call speakers, or task creators. Keep a single named person together even if their name contains a comma or and. Exclude negated people. For other content categories return an empty list and retain unsupported filter wording in query.
search.search_in: Names of channels explicitly requested as the scope of a message or call search. Keep each channel name intact, including commas and and. A year or a preposition inside the topic is not a channel filter. For other content categories return an empty list and retain unsupported filter wording in query.

email.subject: A short phrase from the outgoing message suitable for its subject. It need not be labeled Subject; use the message's main topic or requested action.
email.body: The entire outgoing email message, including every sentence and line. Exclude only the leading instruction that addresses the email. Preserve the author's words.
email.recipients: Names or email addresses explicitly addressed after email or email to at the beginning of the draft. Do not include people mentioned only in the message body.

note.title: The document heading or a short title phrase from the note.

task.title: The first line of the task draft, without an instruction to create a task.
task.body: The complete task description after its title. Include all description sentences and Markdown in input order. Exclude the title and separately stated priority, status, assignee, project or due-date metadata. Null when there is no description.
task.due_date: The task deadline as a date. Null unless a deadline was explicitly supplied. Urgency is not a deadline. Resolve relative days using the reference local calendar.
task.properties: Only explicitly stated values for this task property. Empty when this property was not supplied; do not infer defaults or return other task prose.

calendar.title: The event name, excluding its date, time and location or an instruction to create an event.
calendar.body: Additional event description beyond its name, date, time and location. Null if no additional description was provided.
calendar.start: The event's local start date and time. Resolve relative dates using the reference local calendar. For hours without AM/PM prefer PM for 1 through 7, AM for 8 through 11 and noon for 12. Explicit AM/PM or morning/evening takes precedence. Null when day or time is missing. Determine the event scheduling clause, not a date mentioned as its discussion topic or a negated instruction. Interpret next week as the following Monday through Sunday. Dotted a.m./p.m. are explicit; conversational I am is not a meridiem.
calendar.end: The explicitly supplied event end date and time, or start plus an explicitly supplied duration. Null when neither was supplied; the application provides a one-hour duration.
calendar.location: Physical venue, street address or video meeting platform explicitly named for the event. Null if no location was supplied.
calendar.guests: Only positively requested invitee names or supplied email addresses. Exclude people who must not be invited. A person mentioned as the activity companion, a discussion topic such as guest access, or a negated invitation is not a request to invite them. Return an empty list when no invitation was requested.
calendar.start_assumption: The exact clock phrase whose missing AM/PM required the editable default, such as at 7. Null when AM/PM is explicit (including a.m./p.m.), a 24-hour time was used, or the event daypart is clear from context.

message.body: The entire outgoing chat message, excluding only the leading recipient or channel instruction.
message.recipients: Names of people or channels explicitly addressed by the leading DM or chat instruction.
